'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian conflict (2024–present)|Syrian conflict]]
**[[SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes (2025–present)|SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes]]
***[[2026 northeastern Syria offensive]]
****As part of a [[ceasefire]] agreement with the [[Syrian transitional government|Syrian government]], the [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish]]-led [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] formally hands over control of [[Al-Hasakah]] to [[Syrian Armed Forces|government forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/syrian-government-forces-deploy-towards-kurdish-run-city-after-ceasefire-deal-2026-02-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Blockade of the Gaza Strip]]
***[[Israel]] partially reopens the [[Rafah Crossing]] between [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] and [[Egypt]], which has been closed since May 2024, allowing 150 people to leave Gaza and 50 to enter per day. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/feb/02/israel-agrees-to-limited-reopening-of-rafah-border-crossing-in-gaza (''The Guardian'')]
**At least five people, including a 3-year-old boy, are killed in Israeli attacks according to the [[Gaza Health Ministry]], including two at the [[Nuseirat refugee camp]] and one each in [[Al-Mawasi, Rafah|Al-Mawasi]], [[Khan Yunis refugee camp|Khan Yunis]], and [[Jabalia refugee camp|Jabalia]]. The [[Israeli Defence Forces|Israeli military]] says it targeted "militants operating near the [[Yellow Line (Gaza)|demarcation line]]". [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2026-02-02/ty-article-live/.premium/idf-says-it-struck-hezbollah-militant-in-southern-lebanon/0000019c-1c63-d3f5-a5fd-dc6bd52d0005?liveBlogItemId=430947010#430947010 (''Haaretz'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***Clashes erupt between the [[Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF) and a tribe formerly allied to it in [[East Darfur]]. Prior to the fighting, local sources claim that the tribe abducted relatives of a senior RSF commander over allegations of them allegedly collaborating with the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]]. At least five fighters have been reportedly killed on both sides, including the said RSF commander and the tribe's leader. [https://sudantribune.com/article/310168 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***A [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] drone strike kills two people in [[Stary Oskol]], [[Belgorod Oblast]], [[Russia]]. The [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian Defense Ministry]] says 22 Ukrainian drones were shot down during the overnight attack, which also caused several regional airports to suspend flights. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/02/02/2-killed-after-ukrainian-drone-slams-into-house-in-belgorod-region-a91832 (''The Moscow Times'')]

***[[Japan]] announces it has begun successfully drilling and retrieving deep-sea sediment containing [[rare earth mineral]]s near the remote island of [[Minamitorishima]] in the [[Pacific Ocean]], as the country seeks to reduce its reliance on [[China]] for critical minerals for use in its [[Defense industry of Japan|defense industry]] and [[Automotive industry in Japan|automotive industry]]. *Five workers are killed when an under construction bridge collapses in [[Xiangshui County]], [[Jiangsu]], China. [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3342177/unfinished-bridge-collapses-eastern-china-leaving-2-dead-and-others-missing (SCMP)]

*[[Epstein Files]], [[Relationship of Prince Andrew and Jeffrey Epstein]]
**[[Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor]] leaves [[Royal Lodge]] to move to the [[Sandringham_House#Wider_estate|Sandringham Estate]] as a result of the controversy about his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8e5zgprgn1o (BBC)]
*[[Kidnapping in Nigeria]]
**[[Nigeria]]n [[Nigeria Police Force|police]] state that at least 80 people abducted from [[Christianity in Nigeria|Christian]] churches in [[Kaduna State]] on January 18 return to their homes after fleeing during the abduction, but the [[Christian Association of Nigeria]] disputes the figure and says most of the 177 worshippers seized remain missing. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/nigeria-police-says-80-abducted-congregants-return-home-christian-group-disputes-2026-02-02/ (Reuters)]
